sources.title: Introducing Perceptron Mk1
sources.evidence: Dated May 12, 2026; announces immediate availability of perceptron-mk1 as the first closed model in the Perceptron family. Describes optional reasoning, image/video understanding and grounding. Inspected the three benchmark table images: they report prices and scores, not Mk1 parameter counts.

sources.title: Perceptron Mk1 model guide
sources.evidence: Exact model ID; closed source; text, image and video inputs; text output; 32K context and reasoning. Direct Markdown retrieval succeeded. No total/active count or architecture specification. Tool-calling guidance points to Mk1.5.

sources.title: Mk1 Chat Completions API reference
sources.evidence: The tool_calling_not_supported error example explicitly identifies perceptron-mk1. Shared schema fields require a capable model and do not confer tool support on Mk1. Direct Markdown retrieval succeeded.

sources.title: Perceptron Mk1 changelog
sources.evidence: Explicit May 12, 2026 Mk1 launch entry corroborates the original announcement, including image/video, reasoning and 32K context. Direct Markdown retrieval succeeded.

sources.title: Terms of Use
sources.evidence: July 10, 2026 terms retain Perceptron ownership and grant restricted service access; weight access or self-hosting requires enterprise rights. Supports a descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open-source license.

sources.title: Mk1 MCP integration
sources.evidence: MCP exposes vision operations to external assistants. It does not document Mk1 deciding to invoke tools itself. Direct Markdown retrieval succeeded.

sources.title: Introducing Perceptron Mk1.5
sources.evidence: Later September 25, 2026 release adds audio and tool calling and compares Mk1/Mk1.5 performance and latency. It supplies no total or active Mk1 parameter count. Mk1.5 specifications are not transferred to Mk1.

sources.title: Teaching VLMs to think visually
sources.evidence: June 18, 2026 training and attention study identifies its 9B experimental base as Isaac, not Mk1. It cannot establish Mk1 size or architecture.

sources.title: Composing Weight and Data Sparsity in MoE
sources.evidence: January 21, 2026 research studies Qwen3-based MoE experiments and Isaac comparisons. It does not identify Mk1 as one of those checkpoints, so their topology and counts cannot be transferred.

sources.title: Isaac 0.5: Percepts Scale Control
sources.evidence: Later 52-page first-party report accessed through web PDF extraction. Its Mk1 passage describes a proprietary annotation model; the disclosed 36B total and 2.5B active belong to Isaac 0.5. No Mk1 count or topology is established. Direct local PDF retrieval returned 403; the web tool exposed the report text.

sources.title: Perceptron Mk1 API model page
sources.evidence: Provider documentation specifies its exact Mk1 route at 32,768 context tokens, agreeing with Perceptron’s nominal 32K. Used only for route-level integer precision, not as model-architecture or original-release evidence.

name.note: Exact public name for API ID perceptron-mk1; distinct from Mk1.5.

developer.note: Developer announcement and service terms identify Perceptron.

family.note: The launch explicitly names the Perceptron model family, distinct from its Isaac series.

release_date.note: Actual public launch and same-day API availability; not inferred from a provider listing or catalog timestamp.

open_weights.note: Mk1 is closed source and proprietary. Negotiated enterprise access does not constitute an open-weight release.

license.note: Descriptive classification supported by restricted service/enterprise terms and the report’s explicit proprietary Mk1 designation.

parameters_b.note: No Mk1 total count in the inspected launch tables, exact model guide, later Mk1.5 comparisons or Isaac 0.5 report. Isaac’s disclosed counts describe another model.

active_parameters_b.note: No exact Mk1 active count located in these primary sources. Do not import sparse-model figures from the research experiments or Isaac 0.5.

architecture.note: Vision-language describes function, not topology. Research describes other models; no exact Mk1 Transformer, dense or MoE specification is established.

context_window.note: Developer states nominal 32K; OpenRouter specifies 32,768 for this exact route. Retained as a documented API limit, not independently measured capacity.

modalities.note: Exact Mk1 guide lists these modalities. Grounding annotations are serialized output; audio support belongs to Mk1.5.

reasoning.note: Mk1 documents optional thinking through vision_config.enable_thinking.

tool_call.note: Exact Mk1 API error rejects declared tools and tool-call histories. MCP makes Mk1 callable by other agents; that does not make Mk1 tool-capable.

description.value: Vision-language model for image and video understanding, spatial grounding, and embodied reasoning, with optional thinking.
description.note: Replaces the unsupported planning/tool-use wording with documented visual tasks and optional reasoning.

patch.description: Vision-language model for image and video understanding, spatial grounding, and embodied reasoning, with optional thinking.
patch.notes: Mk1 supports optional reasoning but not function calling; the MCP server lets other agents invoke its vision capabilities. Parameter counts and architecture are undisclosed in the reviewed primary sources. The developer specifies 32K context; its OpenRouter route specifies 32,768 tokens. Mk1.5 specifications do not apply to Mk1.

sources.label: Composing Weight and Data Sparsity in MoE

summary: Audited all 14 fields for exact Mk1. Adds the documented Perceptron family and Proprietary classification, replaces the misleading tool-use description and promotes provenance to the original launch. May 12, 2026, text/image/video inputs, text output, optional reasoning and no tool calling are confirmed. Total/active parameters and architecture remain undisclosed after later comparison and training/interpretability checks; no Isaac or Mk1.5 specifications were imported.
